RATIONALE:
Q1: The group 1 test fails for the same reason as group 3. `review_head_checkout_now_ms` (`scripts/review_autofix_step_checkout_pr_head_branch.sh:40-53`) reads the wall clock with `date +%s%3N`. `review_head_checkout_elapsed_ms` (`:78-93`) subtracts the two readings and never checks for a negative result. So when the runner's clock steps back, `fetch_ms` comes out as something like `-94`. That fails `assert fields["fetch_ms"].isdigit()` at `tests/test_review_checkout_head_diagnostics.py:208`, and it breaks the documented `fetch_ms=<n|na>` contract in `agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-08-review-checkout-diagnostics.md`. The issue's own suggested fix, step 3, asks for the group 1 cause to be found and fixed. Option B would leave a known flaky failure in place. Option C would weaken the contract instead of fixing the cause.
Q2: GITHUB FACTS show #9246 is open and unmerged. Its title mentions only the "heartbeat clock". The test that actually failed checks the `CI_SUBTEST_END` line (`tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py:4669`), not the heartbeat, and #9246's diff is not in this checkout. So it cannot be confirmed that #9246 delivers all of this issue's work, and waiting for it (B or C) would also hold up the checkout-script fix. The smallest self-contained edit, with a check for whatever `main` contains at implementation time, avoids duplicating work and avoids blocking.

Use milliseconds from `/proc/uptime` (integer part of `$1 * 1000`). If that output is not purely numeric, fall back to `date +%s%3N`. Otherwise keep the existing `date +%s%3N` and then `date +%s * 1000` fallbacks unchanged. In `review_head_checkout_elapsed_ms`, clamp a negative END-START or NOW-START result to `0`. Keep printing `na` only when the start value is missing or non-numeric (never started), and keep the existing case where both end and now are non-numeric. Add no new env vars and rename no identifiers.

Cover three cases: (a) end < start gives `0`, not a negative number; (b) a missing start gives `na`; (c) a normal end > start gives the exact difference. Use synthetic integers such as start=`1000`, end=`900` giving `0`, and start=`1000`, end=`1250` giving `250`.
